title: 15-Minute Loaded Black Bean Taco Bowls (When You Refuse to Do Dishes)
description: Fast, flavorful, and zero sink pileup. These easy black bean taco bowls whip up in 15 minutes using canned beans, warm spices, and pantry staples.
story: It was 8:15 PM on a damp Tuesday, and my apartment kitchen sink was already holding a coffee mug and a fork. That was my absolute limit for the night. I live in a fourth-floor walk-up with a tiny half-sized dishwasher that groans if you put more than three plates in it, so the thought of tackling a three-pan dinner made me want to cry. Enter canned black beans. The first time I threw this together, I made the amateur mistake of draining the beans completely dry and blasting the burner on high. The beans turned into dry little rubber pellets in three minutes flat. Now, I keep two tablespoons of that starchy can liquid and simmer them gently in avocado oil with smoked paprika, cumin, and kosher salt. Spooned straight over leftover brown rice with shredded Tillamook cheddar and Aldi salsa, it is dinner in under fifteen minutes. Zero takeout guilt, exactly one nonstick pan to rinse, and I was back on the couch before the show finished buffering.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, keep 2 tablespoons of canning liquid and drain the rest
2 cups warm cooked brown or white rice
1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack or Tillamook sharp cheddar cheese
1 ripe avocado, diced, plus 1/3 cup your favorite salsa for topping
instructions: Step 1: Set a medium nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and add the avocado oil. Add the minced garlic and stir continuously for about 30 to 45 seconds until pale golden and fragrant, making sure it does not scorch.
Step 2: Dump in the black beans along with the 2 tablespoons of reserved canning liquid. Stir in the ground cumin, smoked paprika, and kosher salt until evenly coated.

Step 3: Let the beans simmer gently for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. Take the back of a wooden spatula and lightly smash about a quarter of the beans against the pan floor to build a thick, glossy pan sauce.

Step 4: Take the pan off the heat. Scoop warm rice into two wide bowls, ladle the saucy beans over top, and immediately scatter the shredded cheese over the hot beans so it melts. Crown with diced avocado and cold salsa.
proHack: Do not rinse every drop of bean starch away. Keeping just two tablespoons of the liquid from the bean can and gently crushing a small handful of beans right in the pan creates an instant, velvety pan glaze without needing heavy cream or flour.
storage: Store leftover beans in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat on the stove over low heat with a quick splash of water to loosen the sauce, or microwave for 60 seconds. Assemble with fresh avocado right before eating so it does not turn brown.

faqs.question: Can I substitute black beans if I do not have them in the pantry?
faqs.answer: Yes, canned pinto beans or dark red kidney beans work just as well using the exact same simmer times and spices.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the beans from turning dry and chalky?
faqs.answer: Keep your heat strictly on medium-low and make sure to leave a splash of the can liquid or add two tablespoons of water or vegetable broth while they simmer.
